🚨🦠 H5N1 OUTBREAK ON UTAH MINK FARM — SCIENTISTS WARN OF PANDEMIC RISK!

🇺🇸 UTAH, UNITED STATES | NOVEMBER 12, 2026
⚠️ A DISTURBING INVESTIGATION REVEALS HOW AN AVIAN FLU OUTBREAK WAS ALLOWED TO CONTINUE ON A UTAH MINK FARM WHILE SCIENTISTS WARNED OF POTENTIAL HUMAN HEALTH CONSEQUENCES!

An October 23 investigation by ProPublica journalists Nat Lash and Julie Leopo exposed serious concerns about the handling of H5N1 bird flu at C&T Fenn Farms, a mink operation near Provo, Utah.

State officials learned in mid-August that mink were dying from the virus. By the time ProPublica published its findings, the outbreak had continued for more than two months.

The farm raised thousands of mink for the fur industry.

🦠 WHY ARE MINK SO CONCERNING?

Mink are mammals whose respiratory systems contain cellular receptors relevant to influenza infections in humans.

Scientists fear that continued H5N1 transmission among mink could provide opportunities for the virus to acquire mutations that improve its ability to infect mammals.

Researchers are particularly concerned about the possibility of a future strain capable of efficient human-to-human transmission.

THAT HAS NOT BEEN DEMONSTRATED AT THIS FARM.

🚨 OFFICIAL RESPONSE UNDER SCRUTINY!

ProPublica found that:

🔴 Utah officials did not order the infected mink population culled.

🔴 Federal regulations did not establish the same mandatory response for infected mink as for poultry.

🔴 State authorities did not routinely monitor exposed farmworkers for symptoms.

🔴 Workers were not systematically tested for H5N1.

🔴 A worker reportedly experienced eye redness, a possible bird flu symptom, but was not tested.

🔴 Records showed officials were concerned about the economic consequences of stronger intervention.

Flu experts interviewed by ProPublica sharply criticized the response, arguing that uncontrolled transmission could allow the virus additional opportunities to evolve.

⚠️ WHAT DID VIRAL TESTING REVEAL?

Initial genetic sequencing of infected mink samples did not identify mutations that experts or the CDC considered particularly alarming.

However, scientists wanted updated genetic testing to determine whether the virus had changed during the prolonged outbreak.

The farm owner told ProPublica that additional samples had been collected, but results were still pending at the time of publication.

🔬 COULD THIS TRIGGER A PANDEMIC?

Scientists consider H5N1 a potential pandemic threat because influenza viruses can evolve and occasionally cross species barriers.

But several important distinctions remain:

✅ An H5N1 outbreak among mink was documented.

✅ Experts raised credible concerns about insufficient surveillance.

❌ No confirmed human H5N1 infection was established at this farm in the investigation.

❌ No sustained human-to-human transmission was demonstrated.

❌ No pandemic-capable strain was identified.

A SERIOUS RISK IS NOT THE SAME THING AS A CONFIRMED PANDEMIC.

🌎 THE BIGGER WARNING

The investigation highlights a potential weakness in infectious-disease preparedness: dangerous animal outbreaks may not receive sufficiently coordinated responses from agricultural and public-health authorities.

Experts argue that monitoring animal infections, testing exposed workers, and sequencing viral samples are essential for detecting threats before they spread.

⚠️ NTLD INVESTIGATION — IMPORTANT DATE CLARIFICATION

This ProPublica report was published OCTOBER 23, 2026.

It is not a newly discovered November 12 outbreak.

The latest status of the Utah farm, including whether infections are continuing or have been contained, requires updated official confirmation.

#H5N1 

➡️🇬🇧 England: Bird Flu Outbreak Confirmed at North Lincolnshire Poultry Farm

- A bird flu outbreak has been confirmed at a ➡️ commercial poultry farm near Brigg in North Lincolnshire, with Defra ordering a humane cull of all birds on the premises. The restrictions limit bird movements around the site, while health authorities say the risk to the public remains very low.

- The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said a protection zone of about two miles (3km) and an eight-mile (10km) surveillance zone had been established. The farm is a commercial premises near Brigg.

- All birds at the site will be culled. The protection zone restricts the movement of birds in the area, a measure intended to contain the outbreak and limit further spread from the premises.

- The confirmation adds to cases recorded during the current bird flu season in the UK. The first cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) this season were confirmed in Scotland on 2 October.

WHAT DO THE RESTRICTIONS MEAN FOR NEARBY POULTRY FARMS?

- Bird movements within the protection zone are restricted, while the wider surveillance zone covers an eight-mile (10km) radius around the site. The zones put local poultry operations under movement controls as officials respond to the outbreak.

- ➡️ The virus involved is HPAI H5N1. It can spread through birds’ droppings and saliva, as well as contaminated feed or water. That makes controls around the affected premises relevant to other bird keepers in the area, particularly where birds or their feed and water could be exposed to contamination.

- The cull also carries a direct cost for the affected farm: the birds on the premises will be lost as authorities act to contain the infection. An earlier outbreak in England this season showed the potential scale of that impact. In October, a farmer said losing 32,000 egg-laying birds was likely to cost her business more than £100,000.

- That earlier loss gives a concrete measure of the pressure an outbreak can place on a poultry business, although it concerns a different farm. For the Brigg premises, Defra’s current measure is the removal of all birds, alongside movement restrictions in the surrounding zones.

WHAT IS THE RISK TO PEOPLE AND FOOD?

- The UK Health Security Agency said the risk to the general public’s health from avian influenza remained very low. The Food Standards Agency also assessed the food safety risk as very low.

**No. The ad’s central claim is false.**

Current data shows egg and banana prices are not elevated in the way the ad implies:

- Retail egg prices averaged about $2.27 per dozen in September 2026 (BLS). That is roughly 35% lower than a year earlier and far below the early-2025 peak (over $6 in some periods) driven mainly by Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza outbreaks that reduced flocks. Wholesale prices are even lower (around 30¢/dozen recently).
- Banana prices were around $0.66 per pound in September 2026. They have seen some longer-term increases tied to import costs, tariffs, disease pressures on Cavendish bananas, and shipping/fuel, but they have not spiked because of events involving Israel.

U.S. aid to Israel is about $3.8 billion per year under the long-standing memorandum of understanding ($3.3 billion in Foreign Military Financing plus $500 million for missile defense), with higher totals in 2024 due to emergency supplemental packages after the October 7, 2023 attacks. This is a tiny fraction of the overall federal budget (roughly 0.05% or less in a typical year) and of U.S. grocery spending (over $1 trillion annually). There is no credible economic mechanism by which this aid, or Israeli military operations, meaningfully raises the retail price of U.S. eggs (almost entirely a domestic product affected by disease and production) or bananas (imported from Central and South America).

Broader grocery price pressures in recent years have come from avian flu, cattle herd cycles, weather, labor costs, energy/fertilizer prices (influenced by wider Middle East tensions including the Iran conflict), supply-chain issues, and tariffs—not U.S. security assistance to Israel. The ad’s specific linkage is a non sequitur that does not hold up to the data.

posts.text:
I'm a psychiatrist. I took Xanax for about 6 months. I will never take it again.

It was a hard stretch. Work was crazy and we had a newborn at home. My sleep fell apart, and anyone who's had weeks of insomnia knows how demoralizing it is. It brings you to your knees.

Xanax felt like a miracle at first. Within 20 minutes I was calm and sleeping. Hardly any hangover. That's exactly what makes it a trap.

After about 6 months, it turned on me. I started having intrusive thoughts. Thankfully I recognized it was the drug, came off, and changed my lifestyle to fix my insomnia.

I've spent the last 6 years helping people come off sedatives. Here are the three reasons I tell people to be careful:

1. They're addictive, fast. I hear it every day: "I'm a straight-laced guy, I never even had problems with alcohol, and before I knew it I was hooked." One night becomes several nights a week, because the choice feels like: take the pill, or feel terrible for 16 hours tomorrow.

2. They wear off, and they're hard to stop. After about 2 months, many people find the dose isn't working anymore. Over a few years you can end up on a high dose that barely works. Your brain has adapted, so when you try to stop, you get withdrawal plus the original problem. The FDA now warns that protracted withdrawal symptoms can go on for a year or longer.

3. They can turn on you. It's sometimes called BIND: benzodiazepine-induced neurological dysfunction. More anxiety than before. Avoiding trips and social plans. Mood swings, irritability, constant tension, intrusive thoughts you never had. Some people get ringing in the ears, light sensitivity, tingling, memory problems and brain fog.

The worst part is that it often gets misdiagnosed as a new psychiatric condition, and people end up on more drugs.

If you're already on one of these and you want off, you're not weak and you're not alone. But please don't stop suddenly. Come off slowly with a prescriber, and work on non-drug ways to manage sleep and anxiety.
